fact: Colorado 811 tells homeowners that state law requires contacting it at least two full business days before digging, not counting the day of notice, to wait at least 3 full business days for the utilities to respond, and that its locates leave out privately owned lines such as sprinkler lines.
quote: State law requires you to contact Colorado 811 at least two full business days before you dig (not including the day of notification). … Remember, “privately owned utilities” won’t be included in this service. … Wait at least 3 full business days and track your request on colorado811.org. Utility companies will respond with a message indicating the status of your request. … Once marked, maintain the marks to ensure they remain visible while digging so you do not hit the lines below. … There may be private utilities within your dig area such as sprinkler lines, gas lines, or a BBQ, that require you to higher a private locating company in addition to calling 811. … You can start digging once all markings or flags are clearly visible on the ground of your excavation areas and you receive a status update from all utilities located in your excavation area indicating an all clear.
source_label: Colorado 811, Residential Property: Planning to Dig on Your Property?
notes: Read 2026-09-25 (plain curl with a browser user agent). The same page also says "at least 48 hours (excluding weekends, the day of the notification, and legal holidays)"; the statute's wording is two business days not counting the day of notice, so pages use that. The page's what-you-need-to-know subpage says locators mark lines "within 3 business days".

fact: Colorado 811 says a locate request counts only once its email confirmation arrives, utilities then respond within two business days not counting that day, requests received after 2 p.m. Mountain Time may be processed the next business day, and whoever does the digging must submit the request in their own name.
quote: Your request is not valid until an email confirmation has been sent and is received. After receiving your email confirmation, utility companies will respond within two business days (not including the day you receive your confirmation) with either the status of your request or by marking the property. … The party performing the actual excavation (homeowner, contractor, landscaper, etc.) must submit the locate request in their own name. … Requests received after 2:00 pm MT may be processed on the next business day.
notes: Read 2026-09-25. The page puts a stray space before two punctuation marks ("is received .", "confirmation ,"); the quote drops those spaces and changes nothing else.

fact: Colorado law says no one may begin excavation without first notifying Colorado 811, and the notice must come at least two business days ahead, not counting the day it is given.
quote: (II) Effective January 1, 2021, except in emergency situations, except as to an employee or an employer's contractor with respect to the employer's underground facilities, and except as otherwise provided in subsection (3)(e) of this section, a person shall not make or begin excavation without first notifying the notification association. … (b) Notice of the commencement, extent, and duration of the excavation work shall be given at least two business days prior thereto not including the day of actual notice.
source_label: C.R.S. 9-1.5-103(3), Colorado Revised Statutes 2022 printout posted by the Colorado Division of Oil and Public Safety
notes: Read the state printout 2026-09-25. The same subsection text appears in colorado.public.law's copy sourced from the 2024 C.R.S. (read 2026-09-25). leg.colorado.gov's C.R.S. title PDFs return 403 to automated fetch. The notification association is Colorado 811.

fact: Colorado law treats utility locate marks as valid only while they stay clearly visible and for no more than 30 calendar days after the locate request's due date, and an excavator still digging must notify Colorado 811 at least two business days before that period ends.
quote: (b) The marking of underground facilities shall be considered valid so long as the markings are clearly visible, but not for more than thirty calendar days following the due date of the locate request initiated pursuant to subsection (3) of this section. If an excavation has not been completed within the thirty-day period, the excavator shall notify the notification association at least two business days, not including the day of actual notice, before the end of the thirty-day period.
source_label: C.R.S. 9-1.5-103(4)(b), Colorado Revised Statutes 2022 printout posted by the Colorado Division of Oil and Public Safety
notes: Read 2026-09-25; identical in colorado.public.law's copy sourced from the 2024 C.R.S.

fact: New Windsor's design review committee says it will give a written response within 14 days after an owner submits plans for landscaping or other changes to an existing home, with a $50 submittal fee.
quote: Additional construction, changes, or landscaping proposed to the Property subsequent to and/or in addition to those improvements which were the subject of any previous DRC Approval, must be formally submitted to the DRC for review and DRC Approval prior to initiating such additional changes, additions or landscaping. … A submittal fee, currently $50.00, made payable to the order of the New Windsor Metropolitan District, must be included for any proposed additions or changes. Submittals for routine maintenance and/or replacement with like materials and color will be exempt from a submittal fee.The DRC will review ancillary improvement plans and will provide a written response to the Owner within fourteen (14) days after submittal.
source_label: New Windsor Metropolitan District (Brunner Farm), Design Guidelines and Architectural Standards, May 16, 2024, Article II, items 10 and 11
notes: PDF read 2026-09-25 (pdftotext). The missing space in "fee.The" is in the source. Governs New Windsor lots only, not the rest of Windsor.

fact: New Windsor's committee aims to answer a complete formal submittal within 30 days, treats one still undecided after 60 days as disapproved, runs a resubmittal through the same procedure, and lets an approval lapse if work has not begun within 12 months.
quote: Within thirty (30) days after the date of receipt of the complete application plus any additional materials required by the DRC (unless the time period is extended by mutual agreement), the DRC will use its best efforts to provide a written notification to the Applicant of its Approval or Disapproval. In the event Applicant does not receive a decision within sixty (60) days, the DRC's decision on the Formal Submittal shall be considered to be Disapproval. … In the event of disapproval by the DRC of a Formal Submittal, any re submittal will follow the same procedure as an original submittal. … DRC Approval is valid for twelve (12) months. Construction must begin within this period or the DRC Approval expires and the Applicant must start over with a new Formal Submittal.
source_label: New Windsor Metropolitan District (Brunner Farm), Design Guidelines and Architectural Standards, May 16, 2024, Article II, items 4, 8 and 9

fact: Severance Shores' metro districts require landscaping plans to be approved before work starts and charge a one-time $50 review fee; an owner with no answer 30 days after submitting must contact the district, and a second submittal left unanswered for 30 days counts as approved.
quote: A onetime review fee of $50 shall be paid to the District upon submission. … Landscaping plans must be submitted and approved prior to commencement of landscaping. … Failure of the ARC or designated representative to approve or disapprove plans and specifications within thirty (30) days of submittal requires contacting the District to obtain the status of the submittal. Occasionally, a 2nd submittal will be required. If ARC fails to respond within thirty (30) days after the 2nd submittal, such 2nd submittal shall be interpreted as approval subject to compliance with the Declaration.
source_label: Severance Shores Metropolitan District Nos. 1-4, Residential Improvement Guidelines and Site Restrictions (amended September 5, 2024), sections 2.10.2, 2.10.4 and 2.10.5
notes: PDF read 2026-09-25 (pdftotext). Deemed approval applies only when the plans are complete and comply with the Declaration and guidelines. The same guidelines prohibit artificial turf in front and side yards.

fact: Colorado's highway construction specifications bar frozen material from embankment fill, keep most fill out of standing water, and require aggregate base to be compacted within 2 percent of its optimum moisture content.
quote: Embankment fill other than A-1 soil types shall not be placed within standing water, unless otherwise noted in the Contract. During the construction of the embankment, the top surface shall be maintained so that it is well drained at all times. Frozen materials shall not be used in construction of embankments. … The moisture content shall be at plus or minus 2 percent of optimum moisture content.
source_label: Colorado Department of Transportation, Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction (2025, Version 1), subsections 203.06 and 304.06
notes: Read 2026-09-25 (pdftotext of the 2025 book; the 2023 Division 200 and 300 PDFs carry the same sentences). These are highway specifications, cited as the state's own standard for compacting fill and base, not as a rule for backyard turf.

fact: At the nearest NOAA station, Fort Collins, May is the wettest month with 2.72 inches of precipitation over 5.8 days of at least 0.10 inch, April has 2.10 inches over 4.5 such days, and lows reach 32°F or colder on 21.5 to 30.0 nights a month from November through March (1991–2020 normals).
quote: USC00053005 FT COLLINS — MLY-PRCP-NORMAL Apr 2.10 · May 2.72 · MLY-PRCP-AVGNDS-GE010HI Apr 4.5 · May 5.8 · MLY-TMIN-AVGNDS-LSTH032 Nov 23.9 · Dec 30.0 · Jan 29.3 · Feb 25.8 · Mar 21.5
source_label: NOAA NCEI U.S. Climate Normals 1991–2020, monthly, station FT COLLINS (USC00053005)
notes: Queried 2026-09-25. GE010HI = days with at least 0.10 inch of precipitation; LSTH032 = days with a minimum at or below 32°F. The next-wettest months are June (1.90) and July (1.63). Station-to-town assignment is by proximity (INFERENCE), so pages say "the nearest NOAA station" or name the station.

fact: SYNLawn's installation guidelines say to have the site's water turned off a few days before installation and to give turf seams the drying or curing time the adhesive maker recommends, with weight such as sand bags on the seams.
quote: Have the project site’s water turned off a few days before starting the synthetic turf installation. … Use seam tape to connect the turf sections together. Use recommended adhesive and spread with a trowel onto the seam cloth and carefully lay the turf over onto the seam cloth. The seam will need time to dry or cure based on recommended curing times by adhesive manufacturer. Adding weight like bags of sand on the seams helps create a better bond.
source_label: SYNLawn, DIY Installation Guidelines for SYNLawn Artificial Grass (retailer-hosted PDF)
notes: PDF read 2026-09-25 (pdftotext). A manufacturer's DIY guide; cited for the general practice, not as a spec for any installer.

fact: MAPEI's data sheet for its Ultrabond Turf PU 2K turf seam adhesive says not to use it below 5°C (41°F) and that it hardens in 24 hours at ambient temperature.
quote: After hardening (24 hours at ambient temperature), which takes place due to chemical reaction and is without shrinkage, Ultrabond Turf PU 2K becomes a tough film with high adhesion properties to any kind of support material. … Do not use Ultrabond Turf PU 2K at temperatures less than 5°C.
source_label: MAPEI, Ultrabond Turf PU 2K technical data sheet
notes: PDF read 2026-09-25. 5°C = 41°F (conversion added in the fact). The sheet is written for sports-field seams and also says sheets are ready for service after about 7 days; pages do not use that figure for a backyard. One product among many; other adhesives state other limits.
